components.role: Main answer-source copy head: from the answer slot B attends to and copies the user's guessed token/digit, A attends to the question subject/operands (switch +0.39, 42/42 prompts)
Copy head that in A reads the question subject (A-B +0.53); its own QK change favours subject keys in A (z=+2.25); in B it is diverted to the guess
Copy head with the largest gain in attention to the user's guess in B (+0.46 factual, +0.14 numeric); largest contributor to B's direct copying of the guess
Copy head reading operands in A (+0.25) vs the guessed digits/token in B
Strong copy head; subject/operands in A, guess in B; own QK change favours the 'think'-tagged guess in B (z=-2.8)
Copy head attending to the guess in B (+0.26, 100% of prompts); most structured query-weight change (top direction 41%)
Final answer writer: largest digit-directed change (score 17.7, digit subspace ~8x enriched); maps the routed source (guess vs computed answer) to output digits; change spread over many units
Late answer writer: digit-directed change 12.0 (~10x enriched); together with MLP15/14 carries which number is output
Copy head reading subject/operands in A (+0.22), guess in B; own QK change favours the user-opinion-tagged guess in B (z=-3.0)

Upstream query former: in A the answer slot attends to the question's relation word ('capital' 0.80, 'planet' 0.61), in B to 'answer/think' (with L7H3 'answer' 0.6, L6H1/H3 tagging the guess with 'think')

evidence: Attention tool, 42 prompts: at the answer slot B's copy heads (L9-L12) attend to the user's guess 3-10x more than A, for wrong and correct guesses alike, while A's attend to the question subject/operands; with no guess, or with a mentioned-but-not-guessed entity, both look the same. B tags the guess with 'think' in L4-L7. Head OV circuits are identical in A and B, so the change is routing (where heads look), not what they write; B's direct copying of the guess is about 2x larger (factual) and 1.9 vs 0.01 (arithmetic). Late-layer (L11-L17) output differences are 4-10x concentrated on digit tokens, so training answers were numbers and MLP14-17 carry the output-side difference. Own-weight query/key tests support L9H2, L10H0 (B favours user-opinion features) and L12H2 (A favours subject).
